Network operations (starting a listening server, even in-process) require approval in this sandbox and there's no one available to approve it, so I can't do a live end-to-end check here. The unit tests do fully exercise `renderHtml` (the actual page-generation logic used by `serve`), including the streak numbers, HTML escaping, and the empty-state message — all passing.

## Summary

Added `habit serve [port]`:
- **`src/server.js`** — `renderHtml()` builds an HTML page listing each habit and its current streak (via existing `currentStreak`), with names HTML-escaped; `serve(port = 3000)` starts a `node:http` server that serves that page.
- **`src/cli.js`** — wired up the `serve` command; CLI now only logs a command's result when it's a string, since `serve` starts a long-running server instead of returning text.
- **`test/server.test.js`** — covers streak rendering, HTML escaping, and the no-habits case.
- **`README.md`** — documented the new command.

All 10 tests pass (`npm test`). I wasn't able to do a live browser/curl check since this sandbox denies network operations (server listen, curl) without an approval surface — let me know if you'd like to verify it yourself with `node src/cli.js serve` and a browser.
